The default gateway is the router that forwards traffic to other networks. If it is wrong, local traffic still works but nothing beyond the local network is reachable.

EAP is a flexible framework that supports many authentication methods, such as EAP-TLS with certificates, inside one standard exchange. PAP and CHAP are single fixed methods, and RADIUS is the server that processes the authentication, not the framework itself.

Incident response is the process of identifying a security event, analyzing what happened, and taking action to contain and resolve it. Scanning and risk assessment happen before an incident, and training is preventive education.

Bluetooth is the short-range wireless technology used to pair headphones, mice, and keyboards. A Wi-Fi card connects to a network and an Ethernet card needs a cable, neither of which pairs Bluetooth peripherals.

Application allow listing permits only explicitly approved applications to run and blocks all others by default. A denylist does the opposite, blocking only known-bad programs, while a HIDS only detects suspicious activity.

A dynamic inventory is generated automatically from a source such as a cloud provider, so it always reflects the current set of hosts. A static reservation or a spreadsheet must be updated by hand and quickly goes stale.
Accessories are external peripherals that add functionality, such as a keyboard or mouse. The motherboard, CPU, and power supply are core internal components required for the computer to run.

Programs and Features lists installed applications and provides the uninstall option. Device Manager manages hardware drivers, Disk Management manages partitions, and Task Scheduler manages automated tasks.

In IaaS the provider supplies the underlying infrastructure (servers, storage, networking) while the customer manages the operating systems and applications. PaaS adds a managed platform and SaaS delivers finished applications.
A TOCTOU race condition exploits the gap between a security check and the later use of the checked resource. A jailbreak removes restrictions on a mobile device, which is a different issue.

When nearby access points use the same or overlapping channels, their signals interfere and reduce throughput. The fix is to place neighboring access points on non-overlapping channels, such as 1, 6, and 11 in the 2.4 GHz band.

A switching loop lets broadcast frames circulate endlessly between switches, creating a broadcast storm that overwhelms the network. Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) normally prevents this by blocking the redundant path.
A virtual appliance is a network function, such as a firewall, delivered as software running on a virtual machine. A physical appliance is the same function running on dedicated hardware.

A GBIC (gigabit interface converter) is a hot-swappable transceiver that converts between the switch port and fiber-optic cabling. A DNS server resolves names and a patch panel only organizes cabling, neither provides the optical interface.

Packet capture software records network traffic so analysts can inspect packets and trace suspicious activity. A wireless access point provides Wi-Fi connectivity and does not capture or analyze traffic.

A spectrum analyzer displays radio frequency signals across a band, revealing interference from non-Wi-Fi sources that a normal Wi-Fi tool cannot see. A multimeter measures voltage and a tone generator traces cables.

A SIEM (security information and event management) system centralizes log data from many sources and correlates events to spot incidents. DHCP, DNS, and print servers provide network services but do not correlate security logs.
RFID tags are read by radio waves and do not need line of sight, which makes them ideal for tracking items passing through a doorway. QR codes and infrared both require line of sight to work.

A cloud gateway sits at the boundary between the local network and the cloud, routing and securing traffic between the two environments. A repeater only extends Wi-Fi coverage and a file server only stores files.

A Wi-Fi analyzer scans the radio environment and lists nearby wireless networks, including rogue access points that should not be there. A barcode scanner and a storage app cannot detect wireless networks.

The 20+4-pin ATX connector is the main power connector from the power supply to the motherboard, with the extra 4 pins used on newer boards. The SATA cable carries data and the fan header powers only the fan.

A domain-joined computer is managed centrally by a domain controller, which enforces policies and authenticates users. In a workgroup each computer manages its own accounts and there is no central control.

PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) sets the requirements for protecting stored payment card data. HIPAA covers health data, GDPR covers personal data privacy in general, and RBAC is an access-control method rather than a standard.

Fake security warnings, or scareware, use alarming pop-ups to trick users into paying for fake repairs or calling a scammer. Genuine antivirus alerts never demand payment through a pop-up or a phone number.
Disk Management is the Windows tool for creating, deleting, formatting, and resizing partitions. winver only shows the Windows version, and Device Manager manages hardware drivers.

Data masking substitutes sensitive values with realistic fictional data, so the data stays useful for testing without exposing real information. Encryption keeps the real values intact but unreadable without a key, which is not the same as replacing them.
macOS applications are distributed as .app bundles, which the user launches by double-clicking. .exe, .msi, and .bat are Windows file types and do not run natively on a Mac.

A badge reader is a physical control that restricts who can enter a room. Firewall rules, antivirus schedules, and password policies are logical controls that protect data and systems, not physical spaces.

A knowledge base is the shared documentation where solutions are recorded so the whole team can find and reuse them. Email inboxes and device settings are not searchable shared references for the team.

MAC address filtering allows or denies devices based on their unique hardware (MAC) address. An IP reservation assigns a fixed IP address, and SSID broadcasting only controls whether the network name is visible.
A global policy applies organization-wide to all users and devices, unlike a local policy that affects only one machine or an exception that applies to a single case.

License assignment tracks which license is allocated to which device or user so the company stays compliant with the software agreement. Partitioning divides a disk, and storage tiering manages where data is kept.

An IPS sits inline and can drop or block malicious traffic in real time. An IDS only detects and alerts, while Kali Linux is a penetration-testing distribution used to test defenses, not a blocking control.

Bluetooth operates in the 2.4 GHz ISM band, the same band used by many Wi-Fi networks, and hops across channels within it to avoid interference. The 900 MHz band is used by older cellular and cordless phones, not Bluetooth.

In a corporate environment, IT manages company devices through policy, controlling installations to protect security and ensure compliance. Individual employees do not have unrestricted install rights on managed devices.
The root account is the Linux superuser with full administrative privileges over the system. Standard, guest, and read-only service accounts are deliberately limited to reduce risk.

Change management requires documenting the scope of a change and its risks before it is approved and carried out, so surprises are minimized. Incident management reacts to outages, and problem management finds root causes after the fact.

The form factor, such as ATX, Micro-ATX, or Mini-ITX, defines the motherboard's dimensions and mounting layout, so it must match the case. The socket type determines CPU compatibility, not physical size.

Authentication and system logs record login successes, failures, and the source of each attempt, which is exactly what a SIEM needs to spot brute-force or credential attacks. Email signatures and mouse movements carry no login data.

A bug bounty program rewards external researchers for responsibly reporting vulnerabilities they find. An internal penetration test uses the company's own staff, and a tabletop exercise is a discussion-based rehearsal, not a live hunt for flaws.
Stolen credit card data is sold for money, so financial gain is the classic motivation for this kind of crime. Improving security or meeting compliance are defender goals, not attacker motivations.

Good customer service starts with active listening and empathy, which calms the user and gathers the details needed to diagnose the issue. Jumping to a reinstall or blaming the user skips diagnosis and damages trust.

Garbled output of random characters usually means the printer is receiving data it cannot interpret, most often because the wrong or corrupt driver is installed. An empty tray stops printing entirely, and low toner causes faded prints, not garbled ones.

Changing default credentials and enabling strong Wi-Fi encryption are foundational defenses that stop the most common attacks on a home network. Leaving defaults in place or removing the password does the opposite.

Wire cutters cut cable to length and, combined with a stripper, remove the outer jacket so the wires can be terminated. A multimeter measures voltage and continuity, and a tablet or hard drive is not a cable tool.

Proactive monitoring continuously checks device availability and performance and alerts administrators the moment something fails, minimizing downtime. Waiting for user reports means the problem has already affected people.

The kernel is the core of the operating system: it manages the CPU, memory, and hardware and lets applications run. Browsers and word processors are applications that run on top of the operating system.

The Policy Engine is the decision point in zero trust: it checks each request against policy, identity, and context, then grants or denies access. A honeypot lures attackers and a scanner finds vulnerabilities, neither makes access decisions.
A failing power supply can deliver unstable power, causing sudden random reboots even when the system is idle. A bad shortcut or a full recycle bin affects software behavior, not power stability.

Hibernate writes the contents of memory to disk and powers the computer off completely, using no battery, and restores the session on the next boot. Sleep keeps memory powered, so it still drains the battery.

VA (vertical alignment) panels are known for high contrast and deep blacks, which makes them a popular choice for video viewing. TN panels are fastest but have weaker contrast, and IPS panels excel at color accuracy and viewing angles.
RAM holds the data of running applications, so when it fills up the system slows down or starts swapping to disk. Adding RAM lets more applications stay open at full speed.

Layer 1, the Physical layer, defines the electrical signals, cables, and connectors that carry bits between devices. Layer 3 handles routing, Layer 4 handles end-to-end transport, and Layer 7 provides services to applications.

Power Options controls power plans, including what the computer does when the lid closes, when it sleeps, and how it uses the battery. User Accounts manages accounts and System shows hardware information.

A web filter checks requested URLs against blocklists and categories and prevents access to known malicious or inappropriate sites. An email gateway filters mail, and encryption protects stored data rather than web browsing.

A clear issue description is the foundation of good incident documentation: it states the symptoms, the affected system, and the impact so anyone can follow the ticket. Opinions and unrelated details do not help resolve the problem.

A managed switch can be configured and monitored remotely, supporting features such as VLANs, port security, and traffic monitoring. An unmanaged switch is plug-and-play with no configuration, and a hub simply repeats traffic to all ports.

Jobs stuck in the queue usually mean the printer is paused or offline, or the print spooler service has stalled. Checking the printer status and restarting the spooler is the quick, non-destructive first step before replacing hardware.

Change management requires that changes to critical hardware be reviewed and approved in advance, with the impact assessed and a rollback plan ready. Making the change silently risks an unplanned outage with no way back.

Tokenization replaces sensitive data with random tokens that are meaningless on their own; the real values are kept separately in a secure token vault. Hashing and encryption both derive their output from the original value, which is not the case with tokens.
Layer 3 (Network) handles logical addressing using IP and routes packets between different networks via routers.
The PSU converts AC from the wall into the DC voltages (+3.3V, +5V, +12V) required by internal components.
A MitM attack positions the attacker between two parties, allowing them to eavesdrop, intercept, or alter messages in real time.
The CIA Triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability — is the foundational model of information security.
Laptops use SO-DIMM, which is physically smaller than DIMM modules used in desktops.
RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives. It offers redundancy but no performance gain from striping.
A BIOS reset during a power outage can change the boot order. Verifying and correcting the boot order is the quickest first step.
Class C networks default to a /24 subnet mask (255.255.255.0), providing up to 254 usable host addresses.
VGA transmits only analog video. HDMI and DisplayPort carry both audio and video; DVI-D is digital-only.
Thermal paste fills microscopic surface imperfections, eliminating air gaps that act as insulators and dramatically improving heat conduction.
SATA uses a 7-pin data cable for data transfer and a separate 15-pin power cable for power delivery.
DHCP (port 67/68) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS server addresses to clients.
Device Manager (devmgmt.msc) shows all installed hardware and flags driver errors with a yellow exclamation mark or a red X.
Spear phishing is a targeted phishing attack directed at a specific individual, often using personalized information.
RSA is an asymmetric algorithm using a public/private key pair. AES and 3DES are symmetric; SHA-256 is a hash function.
A firewall is a preventive control because it blocks unauthorized traffic BEFORE it reaches a target system.
Modern CPUs use an 8-pin EPS/ATX12V connector for dedicated CPU power, while the motherboard itself uses the 24-pin ATX connector.
Low or depleted toner in the cartridge is the most common cause of faded output. Shaking the cartridge can temporarily redistribute remaining toner.
LGA sockets have pins on the motherboard socket; the CPU has flat contact pads. Intel desktop CPUs (e.g., LGA1700) use this.
MFA requires at least two of three factor types — something you know, have, or are — making compromise significantly harder.
bootrec.exe with /fixmbr and /fixboot, run from WinRE, repairs the MBR and boot sector.
GPT supports volumes larger than 2 TB and allows up to 128 primary partitions on Windows with UEFI.
NTFS supports large volumes, file-level permissions, EFS encryption, journaling, and compression.
USB 3.2 Gen 2 runs at 10 Gbps. Gen 1 is 5 Gbps, and USB4 can reach 40 Gbps.
An anti-static wrist strap continuously drains static charge from the body to ground, preventing ESD damage.
Dual-channel mode requires RAM in matching (same-colored) slots — typically A1+B1 or A2+B2 per the motherboard manual.
FIDO2 hardware security keys provide phishing-resistant MFA — the physical key is required alongside credentials.
A Trojan masquerades as useful software to trick users into installing it, then performs unauthorized actions.
A pen test simulates real-world attacks to find and validate vulnerabilities for proactive remediation.
TPM is a dedicated security chip storing cryptographic keys and certificates. Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0; it enables BitLocker.
SFC (System File Checker) scans protected files and replaces corrupt or missing files from a cached copy.
Lithium-ion batteries have limited cycle life. If the adapter is confirmed working and the battery won't charge, replace the battery.
VLANs logically segment a switched network into separate broadcast domains without requiring additional physical hardware.
SSH uses port 22 and provides encrypted terminal access, replacing insecure Telnet.
UEFI replaces legacy BIOS and adds GPT support, Secure Boot, large drive support, and a graphical setup interface.
Hyper-V is Windows' built-in hypervisor. Type-1 and Type-2 hypervisors allow multiple virtual machines on one host.
Ghosting is typically caused by a worn fuser assembly that fails to fully discharge the toner drum, leaving residual images.
POST beep codes related to RAM indicate memory errors, often from improperly seated or incompatible RAM modules.
diskmgmt.msc opens Disk Management for creating, deleting, formatting, and managing disk partitions.
Least privilege limits user rights to only what is needed for their role, minimizing damage from errors or attacks.
With a discrete GPU, the monitor must connect to its port, not the motherboard's integrated video output.
Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) consolidates Application, Security, and System logs for diagnosing crashes and errors.
NVMe M.2 uses PCIe (~3.5 GB/s+); SATA M.2 uses the SATA interface (~550 MB/s). The spec sheet indicates the protocol.
A zero-day is a security flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch, making it especially dangerous.
Cracked glass produces sharp fragments. Safety glasses protect eyes and cut-resistant gloves protect hands.
SQL injection inserts malicious SQL into input fields, manipulating queries to extract data or bypass authentication.

When the pool runs out of leases, new clients cannot obtain an address and fall back to APIPA (169.254.x.x), while existing lease holders keep working.
An upgrade can fail or run poorly if the CPU is below the minimum requirements, so checking compatibility first avoids a failed install and wasted time.
Access denied for one user on one folder, while others succeed, points to that user's permissions on the folder rather than a hardware or network-wide fault.
Local traffic works without a gateway, but traffic to other networks must go through the gateway; a wrong gateway address breaks internet access while LAN access still works.
Deleting or quick-formatting only removes file pointers, so data remains recoverable; sanitization overwrites, degausses, or destroys the media so it cannot be read.
A rule that must apply to everyone, everywhere in the organization needs organization-wide scope; narrower scopes would leave gaps where the rule does not apply.
Adware's hallmark is unwanted advertising, browser changes, and degraded performance; ransomware encrypts files for payment, while rootkits hide and worms self-propagate.
Domain join and BitLocker are Pro features that Home lacks; the N edition only removes media features and does not add them.
Anomaly detection is useful only if deviations from the baseline trigger timely alerts; shutting everything down or ignoring the event defeats the purpose of monitoring.
SIP establishes, manages, and terminates voice-over-IP sessions; SMTP moves email, FTP moves files, and SNMP manages network devices.
The 12V rail powers motors, fans, and high-draw components, while 3.3V and 5V rails mainly power logic circuits and memory.
Dry air lets static charge build up more easily, so low humidity raises ESD risk; high humidity, not low, favours condensation and mould.
Zero Trust assumes no implicit trust and verifies every request; perimeter-only trust assumes anything inside the network is safe.
An evil twin mimics a trusted network name to lure users and steal credentials; a legitimate access point would have a known, authorized hardware address.
Isolating the host contains the infection and stops it spreading to clean systems; deleting files or rebooting does not contain it and can destroy evidence.
UEBA baselines normal user and device behaviour and flags anomalies such as unusual times, places, or devices; signature antivirus and password checks do not baseline behaviour.
Both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth vanishing on one machine points to the local adapter being disabled, switched off, or missing a driver, not to the router or the OS as a whole.
OCSP queries a responder for a single certificate's live revocation status, while a CRL requires downloading the whole list of revoked certificates.
The fault is isolated to one host after the cable and jack were ruled out and other hosts are stable, which points to that host's own network interface hardware.
AH provides authentication and integrity checking for IP packets without encryption; ESP adds encryption, IKE negotiates keys, and GRE is a tunnelling protocol.
The ISP-assigned WAN address is globally routable, while 192.168.x.x and 10.x.x.x are private ranges and 169.254.x.x is link-local, none of which route on the internet.
Laser printers produce fast, low-cost-per-page black-and-white text at high volumes; inkjets cost more per page at volume and dot-matrix is slow and low quality for office documents.
Replication keeps a live copy of data at another location for failover and availability; encryption protects confidentiality, tokenization substitutes data, and sanitization destroys it.
A cable stripper removes the jacket cleanly without damaging conductors, and a cable tester then verifies pinout and continuity; the other pairs do not perform both jobs.

A punchdown tool pushes each conductor into the 110 block's blades and trims the excess; a stripper only removes jacket, a crimper is for RJ45 plugs, and a soldering iron is not used for this termination.
Force Quit ends only the frozen application, leaving the rest of the system running; reinstalling the OS or cutting power is excessive and risks data loss.
IoT devices with known default credentials and no patch path are easily found and compromised, often recruited into botnets; unique passwords and patching would reduce that risk.
A VPN encrypts traffic between the device and the company network, so it cannot be read on an open hotspot; disabling the firewall or using plain HTTP does the opposite.
A vendor risk assessment reviews the third party's controls, compliance, and incident history before data is shared; price or branding says nothing about security risk.
The methodology starts by identifying the problem through gathering information and questioning the user; theories, solutions, and documentation all come later.
A UPS provides battery power during brownouts and blackouts, while a surge suppressor only clamps voltage spikes and a power strip provides no backup power.
Dynamic analysis observes code while it runs in a controlled environment; static analysis examines code without executing it.
Physical controls deter or prevent physical access to facilities and hardware; technical controls are implemented in software or hardware logic, and managerial controls are policies and procedures.
Cutting power stops short circuits and limits corrosion from the liquid; heat, shaking, or powering on again can spread the liquid and cause further damage.
An installer that reports insufficient space is blocked by storage, not memory or networking; verifying free space confirms the cause before freeing space or choosing another drive.
The 5 GHz band offers higher speeds and less crowding at short range, while 2.4 GHz reaches farther but is slower and more congested.
Authentication verifies identity; authorization then decides what that verified identity is allowed to do, and accounting records the activity.
Change management requires a documented request with scope and risk analysis approved before work starts, so impacts are understood and stakeholders are informed.
A phishing simulation measures how likely users are to fall for phishing so training can be targeted; it is an awareness exercise, not a punishment or a blocking control.
Once a theory is confirmed, the methodology moves to establishing a plan of action and implementing the solution; documentation and verification follow after the fix.
Powering off prevents further damage and injury, and removing paper along its normal path avoids tearing it further or damaging rollers and sensors.
macOS manages per-app access to the camera, microphone, and other sensitive resources under Privacy & Security settings, where each app's permission can be toggled.
A trap is an unsolicited notification sent by an agent to the manager when an event occurs; GET and SET are manager-initiated requests, not spontaneous alerts.
A site-to-site VPN permanently connects two networks at the gateway level; a client-to-site VPN connects an individual remote user, not whole offices.
Hypervisors need the CPU's hardware virtualization extensions enabled in firmware; Hyper-Threading and Turbo Boost improve performance but do not enable virtualization.
Releasing the old lease and renewing requests a new address from DHCP for the new subnet; formatting or replacing hardware does not fix a stale lease.
Professional communication sets clear expectations about timing and next steps, which keeps the customer informed; slang, oversharing, or silence erodes trust.
A jump server is a hardened, monitored gateway that admins connect to first before reaching internal systems, so internal servers stay hidden from direct internet access.
A hypervisor runs multiple isolated virtual machines on one host, each with its own OS; dual-booting runs only one OS at a time and storage alone runs no OS at all.
Secure Boot verifies that the bootloader is signed by a trusted key before allowing it to run, blocking unsigned or tampered boot code; Fast Boot only speeds startup.
A fault isolated to one application points to that application's installation or files, so repairing or reinstalling it is the targeted fix; hardware replacement does not match the symptoms.
DDR generations are not interchangeable because of different notches and voltages, and desktops use full-size DIMMs while laptops use smaller SO-DIMMs.
Life-cycle management requires documentation and inventory to reflect what is actually deployed, so future troubleshooting and planning use accurate information.
A flow data analyzer aggregates NetFlow or sFlow records into historical reports on top talkers and protocols; a packet sniffer captures live packets and a port scanner only probes open ports.
The local firewall blocks inbound traffic by default, so a new application needs an allow rule; disabling security software or reinstalling the OS does not target the blocked port.
Poor first-layer adhesion and warping are usually caused by an unlevel or incorrectly heated bed; toner and networking are unrelated to 3-D printing.
A multimeter measures voltage, current, and resistance, so it can verify an adapter's output; a cable tester checks wiring, a loopback plug tests ports, and a toner probe traces cables.
An insider threat comes from someone with authorized access misusing it; external attacks and natural disasters do not involve a trusted employee's misuse.
A load balancer distributes traffic across healthy servers and removes failed ones from rotation; a firewall filters traffic and an IDS only detects, neither distributes load.
MMC hosts snap-ins such as Device Manager, Disk Management, and Event Viewer in one console; Task Manager manages processes and Registry Editor edits settings, neither hosts these snap-ins.
Vishing (voice phishing) uses phone calls. Pretexting creates a fabricated scenario — vishing often uses pretexting.
System Restore reverts system files, drivers, and registry to a restore point while leaving personal files untouched.
Swollen or leaking capacitors indicate failure. They cannot be safely or reliably replaced in the field; the motherboard should be replaced.
BitLocker encrypts entire volumes at the disk level. EFS encrypts individual files. BitLocker protects against physical theft of the drive.
Device Manager reveals whether the trackpad is disabled, missing a driver, or reporting an error. This is the logical next diagnostic step.
NVMe SSDs connect via PCIe lanes — most commonly through an M.2 slot on the motherboard or as a PCIe add-in card (AIC).
NVMe uses PCIe lanes and achieves speeds of 3,500+ MB/s, while SATA III maxes out at ~550 MB/s. Speed is the primary advantage.
Many USB expansion cards require a supplemental power connection (Molex or SATA) to supply sufficient current for connected peripherals.
Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) shows running processes, resource usage, startup items, and lets you end unresponsive tasks.
Windows 10 Home 64-bit officially supports up to 128 GB of RAM. Pro and Enterprise support even more (up to 2 TB on some editions).
100% disk usage is commonly caused by failing HDD sectors, Windows Search indexing, antivirus scans, or background updates hammering the disk.
The front panel header is a small block of pins where power switch, reset, HDD LED, and power LED connectors plug in. It is documented in the motherboard manual.
RIP uses hop count as its sole metric and treats any destination more than 15 hops away as unreachable.
CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED indicates a core Windows process terminated unexpectedly. Common causes are corrupt system files, failing RAM, or a dying boot drive.
An IDS passively monitors and alerts (detect-only). An IPS actively blocks malicious traffic in-line.
NAT translates private (RFC 1918) IP addresses to public IPs, allowing multiple internal hosts to share a single public IP.
Salting appends a random value to each password before hashing, ensuring identical passwords produce different hashes and defeating rainbow tables.
SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) aggregates logs, correlates events, and generates alerts for security incidents.
The incident response process: Preparation → Identification/Detection → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Lessons Learned.
The CMOS battery (CR2032) keeps the BIOS/UEFI configuration and real-time clock powered when the computer is unplugged. A dead CMOS battery causes lost BIOS settings.
Feature Updates are the major biannual releases that add new functionality. Quality Updates are the monthly cumulative security patches.
Risk transference shifts financial impact to a third party (insurance company) without eliminating the risk.
Task Manager's Startup tab shows all programs configured to start with Windows and allows you to enable or disable them.
ping tests basic IP connectivity using ICMP echo requests. tracert traces the route; nslookup queries DNS; ipconfig shows adapter configuration.
DLP monitors, detects, and blocks unauthorized transmission of sensitive data on endpoints and across the network.
802.11ac introduced MU-MIMO, operates only on 5 GHz, and achieves theoretical speeds up to ~3.5 Gbps.
A honeypot is a decoy system that attracts attackers, observes their techniques, and gathers threat intelligence.
Type 1 (bare metal) hypervisors like Hyper-V, ESXi, and Xen run directly on hardware. Type 2 (hosted) like VMware Workstation run on top of a host OS.
Display Settings allows you to choose between 'Duplicate' (mirror) and 'Extend' (independent desktop across multiple monitors).
DNS cache poisoning injects fraudulent DNS records, redirecting users to attacker-controlled servers.
Mechanical hard drives with spinning platters and moving read/write heads can produce grinding or clicking noises when failing. SSDs are silent.
Restart-Computer is the PowerShell cmdlet for rebooting a local or remote system. shutdown /s is CMD syntax for shutdown (not restart).

An SSD stores data in flash memory with no spinning platters or read/write heads, so it boots and loads files far faster than an HDD and is more resistant to shock.
An SFP module plugs into a switch port and converts between electrical and optical signals for fiber links; different SFPs support different fiber types and distances.
NFC works only within a few centimetres, so a metal case or excess distance easily blocks it, while Bluetooth and Wi-Fi operate over much longer ranges.
Data masking substitutes realistic fake values for sensitive fields, so developers can test with lifelike data without exposing real personal information.
Vishing is voice-based phishing: the attacker uses a phone call and a fabricated pretext to trick the victim into revealing credentials or other sensitive information.
A toner probe pair injects an audible tone onto a wire at one end and detects it at the other, letting a technician identify a specific cable in a bundle.
Multicast sends one stream to a group address, and only hosts that subscribed to the group receive it, saving bandwidth compared with sending a separate unicast copy to each viewer.
When two hosts are assigned the same IP address, each intermittently claims it and the other loses connectivity, which is the classic symptom of an address conflict.
A laser printer uses toner powder fused onto paper by a heated fuser; if the fuser fails, toner stays loose and smears, and pages emerge warm.
IaC treats network and infrastructure configuration as code in version control, making deployments repeatable, reviewable, and automatically reproducible.
Microwave ovens and neighbouring access points on the same channel emit competing signals in the 2.4 GHz band, degrading wireless throughput even when signal strength looks adequate.
An optical power meter measures received light power in dBm, revealing whether loss along the fiber is too high for the receiver, whereas an OTDR locates faults along the run.
A guest network isolates visitors on a separate SSID/VLAN with internet-only access, preventing them from reaching internal resources.
Ransomware attacks that demand cryptocurrency from unrelated victims are driven by profit; espionage would target specific secrets, and hacktivism would aim for a public message.
A SOHO router combines routing, NAT, DHCP, switching, and Wi-Fi in one device, which is exactly what a small or home office needs.
In a domain, computers join a centrally managed directory, so authentication, policy, and access control are administered from domain controllers rather than per machine.
Multitenancy means multiple tenants share the same physical infrastructure while remaining logically isolated from one another, which is how public cloud providers operate.
SASE combines networking and cloud-delivered security services at the edge, so policy follows users and devices anywhere instead of depending on a central office appliance.
Effective customer support means adapting to the user's level, using clear non-technical language, listening fully, and confirming understanding before acting.
An ADF pulls pages from a stack one at a time through the scanner, allowing multi-page documents to be scanned or copied without manual page-by-page placement.
NAC evaluates a device's health and identity at connection time and grants, restricts, or denies access based on compliance, quarantining devices that fail the checks.
Patch management is the systematic testing and deployment of vendor updates; without it, known vulnerabilities remain exploitable long after a fix exists.
IoT devices such as smart thermostats and cameras are often shipped with weak defaults and rarely patched, making them a common entry point when placed on a business network.
Fiber-optic service transmits data as light, delivering high symmetrical speeds and low latency, unlike DSL and cable, which are asymmetric, or satellite, which has high latency.
dig performs detailed DNS queries, can target a specific server, and displays the full answer, authority, and timing information that ping and traceroute do not provide.
A statement of work defines the specific scope, deliverables, schedule, and terms of a project, whereas an SLA defines ongoing service performance levels.
A SIEM aggregates and correlates logs from many sources in real time, enabling detection of attack patterns that no single device's logs would reveal.
Failover automatically switches service to a redundant standby when the primary fails, providing high availability; backups alone do not keep the service running during an outage.
A CNAME record creates an alias for another hostname, so www.example.com resolves to the same address as example.com without needing a second A record.
A punchdown block holds solid-core conductors in insulation-displacement connectors; a punchdown tool presses each wire into its slot, cutting the insulation to make contact.
A print server hosts the shared printer, queues jobs centrally, and distributes the correct driver to clients, which is far more manageable than direct or per-user connections.
After a theory is confirmed, the methodology calls for establishing a plan of action — considering effects and required resources — before implementing the solution.
De-provisioning is the prompt removal or disabling of accounts and access when someone leaves; failing to do it leaves a live account that can be misused.
A point-to-point link connects exactly two endpoints directly, as with a leased line between two sites, unlike multipoint or mesh designs that involve more nodes.
mSATA is the small SATA-based card form factor used in laptops of that era; M.2 NVMe uses a different connector and protocol and is not interchangeable with mSATA.
BitLocker encrypts the entire drive at rest, so the data remains unreadable without the decryption key even if the drive is removed and attached elsewhere.
A stuck queue with pending jobs and no printer error usually means the Windows Print Spooler service has stalled; restarting it clears the blockage without unnecessary hardware changes.
Under GDPR, the right to erasure — the right to be forgotten — lets individuals request deletion of their personal data when it is no longer needed or consent is withdrawn.
An IP helper address (DHCP relay) on the router converts DHCP broadcasts into unicasts forwarded to the DHCP server on another subnet.
A syslog collector receives and stores log messages from many network devices in one place, making central searching and incident review possible.
A surge suppressor clamps brief voltage spikes to protect equipment but provides no battery backup; a UPS is unnecessary when runtime during an outage is not required.
Group Policy applies centrally defined settings to domain computers and users, enforcing configuration consistently across the organisation.

Handling EU and California residents' personal data triggers legal duties under regulations such as GDPR and CCPA, which override internal policy and must shape how data is collected, stored, and deleted.
Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) lets administrators shrink, extend, format, and create partitions and volumes on local disks.
MAC filtering maintains an allowlist of hardware addresses permitted on the network; it is a basic access control, though MACs can be spoofed, so it should not be the only security layer.
Static analysis examines source code or binaries without executing them, finding vulnerabilities early, whereas dynamic analysis tests the running application.
RJ45 is the 8-position, 8-contact modular connector used for Ethernet over twisted-pair cabling; RJ11 is the smaller 6-position connector used for telephones.
Pretexting uses a fabricated scenario and false identity to manipulate a victim into disclosing information; the invented story is the defining feature.
A domain-joined computer authenticates against the domain, receives Group Policy, and enables single sign-on to domain resources, unlike a workgroup machine managed locally.
A KVM switch connects one keyboard, monitor, and mouse to multiple computers, letting an administrator switch control between them without separate peripherals for each.
The kernel is the core of the OS: it schedules processes, manages memory, and mediates all access to hardware, while the shell and GUI are interfaces on top of it.
A USB Ethernet adapter (USB NIC) adds a wired interface through an external port with no disassembly, unlike an internal PCIe card that requires opening the machine.
In a full mesh, each node connects directly to all others, eliminating single points of failure at the cost of many links.
PXE boot lets a computer load a boot image from a network server, enabling large-scale OS deployment without local boot media.
The 24-pin ATX connector (20+4) is the main power connection from the PSU to the motherboard; the 8-pin connector powers the CPU separately.
When multiple routes match, the router chooses the most specific — the longest prefix — so 10.1.0.0/16 wins over 10.0.0.0/8 for 10.1.5.20.
Attenuation is the loss of signal strength over distance; beyond the recommended length the signal becomes too weak for reliable reception, causing errors and retransmissions.
The troubleshooting methodology begins with identifying the problem — gathering information and determining symptoms — before forming or testing a theory.
Smishing is phishing delivered by SMS text message; the fraudulent link and impersonation of a delivery service are the telltale signs.
The Network layer handles logical addressing and routing: routers forward packets based on destination IP addresses, while the Data Link layer uses physical MAC addresses.
XSS injects client-side scripts into web pages served to other users, enabling session hijacking and credential theft.
A CA is the trusted entity that issues, signs, and revokes digital certificates, binding a public key to a verified identity.
POST checks essential hardware — CPU, RAM, GPU, storage — during startup. Beep codes or error messages indicate which component failed POST.
Incorrect keyboard layouts (e.g., AZERTY instead of QWERTY) cause wrong characters. This can be changed in Windows Settings > Time & Language > Language.
A buffer overflow writes beyond a buffer's bounds, overwriting adjacent memory — exploited to execute shellcode or alter program flow.
HTTPS uses port 443. HTTP uses port 80.
An air gap physically isolates a system from all external connections, making remote attacks impossible.
Worms self-replicate across networks without attaching to host files. Viruses require host files; Trojans require user execution; spyware monitors activity.
High idle memory usage is often caused by background services, startup programs, or memory leaks from poorly coded applications.
Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) handles partition creation, formatting, drive letter assignment, and volume extension/shrinking.
STP prevents switching loops by placing redundant ports in a blocking state while maintaining a loop-free path.
A rootkit operates at the kernel or hypervisor level, hiding files, processes, and network connections for stealthy persistent access.
Proper spacing (air gaps) between components inside the case ensures adequate airflow, which is critical for thermal management and preventing overheating.
System Restore rolls back system files, drivers, and registry to a known-good restore point, often resolving issues caused by updates.
MITRE ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary TTPs based on real-world observations, used for threat modeling and detection.
USB-C and USB 3.x ports are the modern standard for connecting external storage devices with high throughput and power delivery.
The chipset (PCH) manages data flow between the CPU, memory, storage, USB, PCIe, and other I/O. It is the motherboard's traffic controller.
Disk cloning software creates an exact replica of the source drive, including the boot sector and hidden partitions, ensuring the new drive is fully bootable.
1000BASE-T requires Cat 5e or better UTP cabling, which supports all four wire pairs at up to 100 m.
Task Manager's Performance tab shows real-time network usage. The Processes tab also shows network usage per application.
A UPS provides battery backup during short power outages, giving the user time to save work and perform a clean shutdown to prevent data loss.
Smishing (SMS phishing) uses text messages to trick victims into clicking malicious links or providing sensitive information.
The BIOS/UEFI boot order must be configured so the USB drive is checked before the internal hard drive. This is done in the Boot menu of the firmware setup.
An A record maps a domain name to a 32-bit IPv4 address. AAAA records map to 128-bit IPv6 addresses.
Each Windows user account has an independent profile containing personal files, desktop settings, and application data, keeping users isolated from each other.
RBAC grants permissions based on predefined roles (e.g., 'HR Manager'). Users are assigned to roles, simplifying permission management.
The Northbridge historically managed high-speed pathways (CPU-RAM-GPU). In modern CPUs, these functions are integrated directly into the processor die.
SHA-256 is a secure hash function from the SHA-2 family producing a 256-bit digest. MD5 and SHA-1 are considered broken for security purposes.
DDoS uses multiple compromised systems (botnets) to flood a target with traffic, exhausting resources and denying service to legitimate users.
A digital signature uses the sender's private key to sign a hash of the message. The recipient verifies with the sender's public key, confirming identity and integrity.
Proper case ventilation with intake fans at the front/bottom and exhaust fans at the top/rear creates airflow that removes hot air and draws in cool air.
ipconfig /release drops the current DHCP-assigned IP. ipconfig /renew sends a new DHCP Discover to obtain a fresh IP address from the server.
Zero trust assumes breach and verifies every access request, regardless of whether the user is inside or outside the network perimeter.

bonus.explanation: MTTR is the average time needed to repair a failed system and restore service; MTBF is the average time between failures, while RTO/RPO are recovery targets.
DLP monitors and blocks sensitive data leaving the organization; NAC controls network access, IPS blocks attacks, and SIEM collects and analyzes security events.
